subproblems.title: Support of an integer multiplicity current equals the support of its weight (Simon 6.2.12 with 6.3.2(3))
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, n ∈ ℕ, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) a current (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n: M ⊆ U Borel, countably n-rectifiable, θ ≥ 1 on M integer valued and locally H^n-integrable in U, ξ an H^n-measurable unit orientation of the approximate tangent planes H^n-a.e. on M) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). Let μ = θH^n⌞M (R.measure). Then spt T = U ∩ spt μ, where spt μ is the set of points all of whose neighbourhoods have positive μ-measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration: this is the already comparator-accepted theorem imrep_represents_support_eq_inter_measure_support (DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.imrep_support_eq_measure_support-a1, status accepted with a candidate commit), reused here by Lean name with its byte-identical frozen Lean type, so no new node and no new proof work is created; listing it as a child makes the controller overlay its accepted history into the dependent siblings, whose frozen proof base (the pristine dispatch commit) does not contain it. In the present decomposition it supplies fact (Supp) of the parent-supplied proof, spt C = spt μ (used with U = ℝ^P by the sibling gap_ae). The numbered proof below is the one reviewed and accepted for that node, reproduced verbatim.

Source: parent step 1 ("spt C = spt μ"), i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 296–305: spt T = spt μ_T) together with Ch. 6, 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768: μ_T = θH^n⌞M). Simon gives no proof of 3.2(3). Instead of the mass identity M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n (whose proof with the contract's Euclidean coefficient norm would need a Cauchy–Binet comparison of covectors with unit simple n-vectors, not available in Mathlib) we prove both inclusions directly from the integral representation; the inclusion U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T uses the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations, which is exactly the consequence "T vanishes on W ⇒ μ(W) = 0" of 3.2(3) that the parent uses ("if C vanishes on all forms supported in B, M_B(C) = μ(B) = 0").

Notation. M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult (θ ≥ 1 on M), ξ = R.orient, H^n = μHE[n], μ = R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ; thus μ(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dH^n for Borel A and ∫ f dμ = ∫_M θ f dH^n. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support), spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) with spt ω ⊆ W ("T vanishes on W"). spt μ (Measure.support) is the set of x such that μ(N) > 0 for every neighbourhood N of x.

1. Preliminaries.
 (a) Since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ A) ≤ μ(A) for every Borel A; and μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (R.locallyIntegrable_mult).
 (b) For an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P define δ_τ(w_1,…,w_n) := det(⟨τ_i, w_j⟩)_{i,j=1..n}. It is the row-determinant of the n vectors L(w_j) ∈ ℝ^n, L(w) := (⟨τ_i, w⟩)_i, hence n-linear and alternating in (w_j); it is continuous (finite dimension), so δ_τ is an n-covector, and δ_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i,τ_j⟩) = det(I) = 1 (for n = 0, δ_τ is the constant form 1).
 (c) For orthonormal τ and every n-covector α, |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (operator norm). Hence if ξ_0 is a unit orientation of an n-plane (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_0 Q: ξ_0(α) = ±α(τ) with τ orthonormal spanning Q), then ‖ξ_0‖ ≤ 1 and ξ_0(δ_τ) = ±1 ≠ 0.
 (d) By R.orients, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of an n-plane; since μ ≪ H^n⌞M, (c) gives ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 and ξ(x) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. x.
2. spt T ⊆ U ∩ spt μ. Let x ∈ spt T; then x ∈ U. Suppose x ∉ spt μ, so μ(N) = 0 for some neighbourhood N of x. Since U is open, choose ε > 0 with closedBall(x, ε) ⊆ N ∩ U and put W := ball(x, ε). W is open, closure W ⊆ closedBall(x, ε) is compact and contained in U. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. Then ω(y) = 0 for y ∉ W, while H^n(M ∩ W) ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(N) = 0 by 1(a). Hence y ↦ θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) vanishes H^n-a.e. on M and T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH^n = 0. So T vanishes on W, i.e. x ∈ W ⊆ Z, contradicting x ∈ spt T = U ∖ Z. Therefore x ∈ U ∩ spt μ.
3. Claim: if W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U and T vanishes on W, then μ(W) = 0.
 Consider f(y) := ξ(y), a function with values in the Banach space Λ_n = MultiVector P n (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors). f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (ξ is for H^n⌞M, and μ ≪ H^n⌞M) and ‖f‖ ≤ 1 μ-a.e. by 1(d); since μ(W) ≤ μ(closure W) < ∞ by 1(a), f is integrable on W, in particular locally integrable on the open set W. Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and spt g ⊆ W, and put I_g := ∫ g f dμ ∈ Λ_n. For every n-covector α the form ω := gα (ω(y) = g(y)·α) is C^∞, compactly supported, spt ω ⊆ spt g ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and T(ω) = 0; evaluation at α is a continuous linear functional on Λ_n and commutes with the Bochner integral (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply / integral_comp_comm), so, by the representation and linearity of ξ(y),
 I_g(α) = ∫ g(y) ξ(y)(α) dμ(y) = ∫_M θ(y) ξ(y)(g(y)α) dH^n(y) = R.action(ω) = T(ω) = 0
 (the middle equality is ∫ F dμ = ∫_M θ F dH^n, Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul). Hence I_g = 0 for all such g. By the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations on an open set, for functions with values in a complete normed space (Mathlib IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero, which needs no local finiteness of μ), ξ(y) = f(y) = 0 for μ-a.e. y ∈ W. (Equivalently one may test against the members of a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors; that space embeds linearly and injectively into the finite-dimensional space of n-linear maps, Mathlib Module.Finite for multilinear maps.) By 1(d), ξ(y) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. y. Therefore μ-a.e. point lies outside W, i.e. μ(W) = 0.
4. U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T. Let x ∈ U ∩ spt μ and suppose x ∉ spt T, i.e. x ∈ Z; then x ∈ W for some open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, on which T vanishes. By step 3, μ(W) = 0; but W is an open neighbourhood of x and x ∈ spt μ, so μ(W) > 0. Contradiction; hence x ∈ U ∖ Z = spt T.
5. Steps 2 and 4 give spt T = U ∩ spt μ, i.e. T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support.

(Clarification of references inside the reproduced proof, not a change of argument: "parent step 1" and "the parent" refer to the original parent of that accepted node, DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1; in the present decomposition the theorem is used only through its stated conclusion T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support.)
proof_key_steps: θ ≥ 1 on M: a μ-null ball meets M in an H^n-null set, so T vanishes on it; hence spt T ⊆ U ∩ spt μ.
For g ∈ C^∞_c(W): (∫ gξ dμ)(α) = T(gα) = 0 for every covector α, so ∫ gξ dμ = 0 and the (Banach-valued) fundamental lemma gives ξ = 0 μ-a.e. on any W on which T vanishes.
ξ ≠ 0 μ-a.e. (ξ(δ_τ) = ±1 for δ_τ = det(⟨τ_i,·⟩)), so μ(W) = 0 for every piece W of the zero region; hence U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T.

Then for every λ > 0 and every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P, μ(λA) = λ^n μ(A), where λA = {λa : a ∈ A}.

The numbered proof below is the one reviewed and accepted for that node, reproduced verbatim.

Source: parent step 3, first half: "IsConeCurrent C gives η_{0,λ#}C = C for λ > 0; the mass measure of η_{0,λ#}C is λ^{−n}(η_{0,λ})_#μ (area formula for the homothety), so μ(λA) = λ^nμ(A) for Borel A" — Simon 7.4.5, proof line 698 ("by virtue of the fact that C is a cone", chapter-07.txt lines 697–699), push-forward Ch. 6, 2.23 (chapter-06.txt line 408) and the push-forward of integer multiplicity currents by the area formula Ch. 6, 3.3–3.6 (chapter-06.txt lines 770–830), and the representation independence of the mass measure, which is the sibling imrep_measure_unique (Simon 6.3.2(3)).

Notation. M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, H^n = μHE[n], μ = R.measure. Fix λ > 0 and put S(y) := λ^{-1}y; for a set A, λA := {λa : a ∈ A} = (x ↦ λx) '' A.
1. Scaling of H^n. For every set B and c > 0, H^n(cB) = c^n H^n(B) (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). Consequently the push-forward of H^n⌞M under the homeomorphism S is λ^n·H^n⌞S(M): for Borel B, H^n(M ∩ S^{-1}(B)) = H^n(λ(S(M) ∩ B)) = λ^n H^n(S(M) ∩ B). Hence for every function F on ℝ^P (Bochner integral, or lower integral of F ≥ 0):
 (1.1) ∫_{S(M)} F dH^n = λ^{-n} ∫_M F(S(y)) dH^n(y),
 using the change of variables formula for the measurable embedding S (Mathlib integral_map_equiv / lintegral_map_equiv) and linearity in the measure.
2. The cone identity in terms of forms. For an n-covector α and c ∈ ℝ, α∘(c·id) = c^n α (multilinearity: α(cv_1,…,cv_n) = c^nα(v)). By the contract, blowUp C 0 λ is the push-forward of C by the proper affine map η(y) = −λ^{-1}·0 + λ^{-1}y = S(y), acting by (blowUp C 0 λ)(ω) = C(η^#ω) with (η^#ω)(y) = ω(S(y))∘(λ^{-1}id) = λ^{-n}ω(λ^{-1}y) (affinePullbackForm with L = λ^{-1}id, b = 0); η^#ω is again a test form because η is a proper affine isomorphism. The domain of blowUp C 0 λ is dilation 0 λ '' univ = univ, so every test form ω on ℝ^P satisfies the test-form condition in currentEval, and IsConeCurrent C gives
 (2.1) C(ω) = C(η^#ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P).
3. The rescaled triple R_λ := (M', θ', ξ') with M' := S(M) = λ^{-1}M, θ'(z) := θ(λz), ξ'(z) := ξ(λz) is an IMRep univ n:
 - M' is Borel (image of a Borel set under the homeomorphism S) and M' ⊆ univ.
 - M' is countably n-rectifiable: if M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n) with H^n(M_0) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz, then M' ⊆ S(M_0) ∪ ⋃_j (S∘F_j)(ℝ^n), H^n(S(M_0)) = λ^{-n}H^n(M_0) = 0, and S∘F_j is Lipschitz.
 - θ' is measurable and θ'(z) = θ(λz) > 0 for z ∈ M' (since λz ∈ M).
 - For compact K: ∫_{M'∩K} θ' dH^n = λ^{-n} ∫_{M∩λK} θ dH^n < ∞ by (1.1) (M' ∩ K = S(M ∩ λK)) and the local integrability of θ on the compact set λK.
 - ξ' is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M': the map z ↦ λz carries H^n⌞M' to λ^{-n}·H^n⌞M (by step 1), so composing the H^n⌞M-a.e.-strongly measurable ξ with it gives an H^n⌞M'-a.e.-strongly measurable function.
 - Orientation: let E ⊆ M be the H^n-null set off which R.orients holds. S(E) is H^n-null by step 1. For z ∈ M' ∖ S(E), y := λz ∈ M ∖ E, so there is an n-plane Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ y) Q. For r > 0, blowUpMap z r '' M' = {r^{-1}(λ^{-1}m − z) : m ∈ M} = {(λr)^{-1}(m − λz) : m ∈ M} = blowUpMap y (λr) '' M, and λr → 0⁺ as r → 0⁺; hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' z Q, and ξ'(z) = ξ(y) is a unit orientation of Q.
4. R_λ represents C. For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), by (1.1) with F(z) = θ(λz)ξ(λz)(ω(z)) and linearity of ξ(y):
 R_λ.action(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ(λz) ξ(λz)(ω(z)) dH^n(z) = λ^{-n} ∫_M θ(y) ξ(y)(ω(λ^{-1}y)) dH^n(y) = ∫_M θ(y) ξ(y)(λ^{-n}ω(λ^{-1}y)) dH^n(y) = R.action(η^#ω) = C(η^#ω) = C(ω),
 the last two equalities by R.Represents C (η^#ω is a test form on ℝ^P) and (2.1).
5. By the sibling imrep_measure_unique (applied with U = ℝ^P, which is open, to the two representations R_λ and R of C): R_λ.measure = R.measure.
6. For measurable A, M' ∩ A = S(M ∩ λA), so by (1.1) R_λ.measure(A) = ∫_{M'∩A} θ' dH^n = λ^{-n}∫_{M∩λA} θ dH^n = λ^{-n}·R.measure(λA). With step 5, R.measure(λA) = λ^n·R.measure(A), i.e. R.measure((x ↦ λx) '' A) = ENNReal.ofReal(λ^n)·R.measure(A).

In the present decomposition it supplies the a.e.-strong measurability of x ↦ p_{T_x} that makes G a.e.-strongly measurable in step 3(b) of the parent-supplied proof (via the sibling fibre_signed). The numbered proof below is the one reviewed and accepted for that node, reproduced verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 3 §1 (T_xM is unique, 1.5(1)) and the definition 6.3.1 of an integer multiplicity current, in which ξ orients T_xM in an H^n-measurable way; this measurability is implicit in Simon's formulas ∫ div_M X dμ_V (Ch. 4, 2.2–2.7) used in steps 2, 5 and 6 of the parent proof.
1. a.e. identification. Let μ := μHE[n].restrict M. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x. At such x the existential in the definition of approxTangentPlane holds, so approxTangentPlane n M x is some Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q'; by uniqueness of approximate tangent planes (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) Q' = Q_x.
2. Case n = 0. Every Q with finrank 0 equals ⊥, and approxTangentPlane 0 M x is ⊥ in both branches of its definition, so the map is the constant 0, which is strongly measurable. Assume n ≥ 1.
3. A unit simple n-vector determines its plane. Let ζ ∈ (Λ^n)^* with ζ(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, τ orthonormal, s = ±1. Claim: span τ = {v : ζ(ι_vβ) = 0 for every (n+1)-covector β}, where ι_vβ(u_1, …, u_n) := β(v, u_1, …, u_n). If v ∈ span τ then β(v, τ_1, …, τ_n) = 0 because the arguments are linearly dependent. If v ∉ span τ, let w := v − Σ_i⟨v, τ_i⟩τ_i ≠ 0 and β(u_0, …, u_n) := det(⟨c_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b=0..n} with c := (w, τ_1, …, τ_n), a continuous alternating (n+1)-form; the matrix (⟨c_a, (v, τ_1, …, τ_n)_b⟩) has first row (|w|², 0, …, 0) and lower-right block I_n, so β(v, τ) = |w|² and ζ(ι_vβ) = s|w|² ≠ 0. Consequently, if ζ orients both Q and Q' (IsUnitOrientationOf) then Q = Q'.
4. Continuity of the orientation-to-projection map. Let Ω := {(τ, s) : τ ∈ (ℝ^P)^n orthonormal, s ∈ {1, −1}}, a compact set, and Φ(τ, s) := (β ↦ s·β(τ)), a continuous map Ω → (Λ^n)^* (multilinear evaluation with |τ_i| = 1). Its image 𝒮 is compact, hence closed, and equals the set of ζ for which ∃ Q, IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q. The map G̃(τ, s) := Σ_i ⟨τ_i, ·⟩τ_i = starProjection(span τ) is continuous on Ω and, by step 3, constant on the fibres of Φ; hence G̃ = G∘Φ for a unique G : 𝒮 → End(ℝ^P). Since Φ : Ω → 𝒮 is a continuous surjection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space, it is a quotient map, so G is continuous on 𝒮. Extend G by 0 outside 𝒮; the extension is Borel measurable (𝒮 closed, G continuous on it).
5. Conclusion. For μ-a.e. x (step 1), ξ(x) = Φ(τ, s) for an orthonormal basis τ of Q_x = approxTangentPlane n M x, hence starProjection(approxTangentPlane n M x) = G(ξ(x)). Since ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and G is Borel, G∘ξ is μ-a.e. measurable; End(ℝ^P) is finite-dimensional (second countable and metrizable), so G∘ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and so is the μ-a.e. equal map x ↦ (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection.

(Clarification of references inside the reproduced proof, not a change of argument: "steps 2, 5 and 6 of the parent proof" refer to the original parent of that accepted node, DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1; in the present decomposition the theorem is used only through its stated conclusion, the H^n⌞M-a.e. strong measurability of x ↦ (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection.)
proof_key_steps: Almost everywhere the approximate tangent plane is the plane oriented by ξ(x) (uniqueness of T_xM).
A unit simple n-vector determines its plane (kernel of v ↦ ζ(ι_v ·)).
The map unit simple n-vector ↦ projection is continuous on the compact set of such vectors (quotient-map argument); compose with the a.e.-measurable ξ.

subproblems.title: Localization yields the sector gap μ-almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ 2), Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with orthogonal projection π = Q.starProjection, a, e ∈ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ 2) representing C (R.Represents C), μ := R.measure, and s > 0. Write f(x) := arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩) and q(x) := x − πx. Assume the localization property Loc(s): for every s' ∈ (0, s] and every x ∈ spt C with ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s' and |q(x)| ≤ 2s|x|, one has |q(x)| < (s'/4)|x| and |x − a| < 3s'. Then for μ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P: if ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s and |f(x)| < s, then |q(x)| < (s/2)|x| or 2s|x| < |q(x)|.

Source: step 1 (Gap) of the parent-supplied proof of idtp_cse_flux_density_eq, together with the fact (Supp) used there. Notation as in the statement; spt C = C.support and spt μ = μ.support (Measure.support: the points all of whose neighbourhoods have positive μ-measure).
1. (spt C = spt μ.) ℝ^P = univ is open and R represents C, so the sibling support_eq (the accepted theorem Submission.imrep_represents_support_eq_inter_measure_support, applied with n = 2, U = univ, T = C, isOpen_univ and R.Represents C) gives C.support = univ ∩ R.measure.support; with Set.univ_inter, spt C = spt μ.
2. (μ is carried by its support.) ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf (Mathlib instance SecondCountableTopology.toHereditarilyLindelof), so MeasureTheory.Measure.support_mem_ae gives μ.support ∈ ae μ: μ-a.e. x lies in spt μ, hence by step 1 in spt C.
3. (Pointwise dichotomy.) Let x ∈ spt C satisfy ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s and |f(x)| < s. If 2s|x| < |q(x)|, the second alternative holds. Otherwise |q(x)| ≤ 2s|x|, and Loc(s) applied with s' := s (admissible because 0 < s and s ≤ s) to x — all of its hypotheses x ∈ spt C, ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s, |f(x)| < s and |q(x)| ≤ 2s|x| hold — yields |q(x)| < (s/4)|x| (first component of its conclusion). Since s > 0 and |x| ≥ 0, (s/4)|x| ≤ (s/2)|x|, so |q(x)| < (s/2)|x|, the first alternative.
4. Filtering the a.e. statement of step 2 through step 3 (filter_upwards) gives the claim for μ-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: spt C = spt μ by the reused accepted support theorem with U = ℝ^P (univ is open).
μ((spt μ)ᶜ) = 0 by Measure.support_mem_ae (ℝ^P is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf).
On spt C: either 2s|x| < |q(x)|, or |q(x)| ≤ 2s|x| and Loc(s) with s' = s gives |q(x)| < (s/4)|x| ≤ (s/2)|x|.

subproblems.title: Consequences of the fibre area identity: finiteness, integrability, signed and box identities
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ 2) with weight μ := R.measure = θ·H²⌞M (H² = μHE[2]), Q a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P with orthogonal projection π = Q.starProjection, a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = 0, and s ∈ ℝ. Put T_x := approxTangentPlane 2 M x with orthogonal projection p_{T_x}, Ax := ⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a, G(x) := |p_{T_x}(Ax)|²/|πx|² (real division, t/0 = 0), f(x) := arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩), F̃(x) := (|x|, f(x)), Z(s,s') := {x : ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s', |x − πx| < s|x|} and Z := Z(s,s). Let H : ℝ² → [0,∞] be a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure with ∫ b(p)H(p) dp = ∫_Z b(F̃(x))·ofReal(G(x)) dμ(x) for every Borel b : ℝ² → [0,∞]. Then (i) H(p) < ∞ for a.e. p; (ii) H_ℝ := toReal∘H is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ²; (iii) for every Borel b : ℝ² → ℝ with sup|b| < ∞, ∫ b(p)H_ℝ(p) dp = ∫_Z b(F̃(x))G(x) dμ(x) (Bochner integrals); (iv) for every s' ≤ s, ∫_{(1−s',1+s')×(−s',s')} H(p) dp = ∫_{Z(s,s')} ofReal(G) dμ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (area identities, parts (a) and (b)) and the first half of step 8 of the parent-supplied proof of idtp_cse_flux_density_eq. Lebesgue measure on ℝ² is volume on ℝ × ℝ; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, toReal = ENNReal.toReal.
1. (Frame bound: G ≥ 0 everywhere and G ≤ 1 on {⟨x,a⟩ > 0}.) G ≥ 0 as a quotient of squares. Let ⟨x,a⟩ > 0 and y := πx. Since π is self-adjoint and πa = a, πe = e (a, e ∈ Q; Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right, Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff), ⟨y,a⟩ = ⟨x,a⟩ and ⟨y,e⟩ = ⟨x,e⟩. Using |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = 0, |Ax|² = ⟨x,a⟩²|e|² − 2⟨x,a⟩⟨x,e⟩⟨e,a⟩ + ⟨x,e⟩²|a|² = ⟨x,a⟩² + ⟨x,e⟩² (norm_sub_sq_real). Bessel's inequality for the orthonormal pair (a, e): with u := ⟨y,a⟩a + ⟨y,e⟩e, 0 ≤ |y − u|² = |y|² − 2⟨y,u⟩ + |u|² = |y|² − (⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩²), so ⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩² ≤ |y|². Also y ≠ 0 because ⟨y,a⟩ = ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, so |y|² > 0. An orthogonal projection does not increase norms (Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le), hence |p_{T_x}(Ax)|² ≤ |Ax|² = ⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩² ≤ |y|² = |πx|², i.e. G(x) ≤ 1 (div_le_one). (The hypothesis dim Q = 2 is not needed here.) In particular 0 ≤ G ≤ 1 on Z.
2. (Measurability.) (a) x ↦ ⟨x,a⟩, ⟨x,e⟩, |x|, ||x| − 1|, |x − πx| and s|x| are continuous; x ↦ ⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩ is Borel (quotient of measurable maps), and arctan and |·| are continuous, so f and |f| are Borel and F̃ = (|·|, f) is measurable. Each Z(s,s') is a finite intersection of sets {u < v} with u, v Borel, hence Borel (measurableSet_lt). Each box Sq(s') := (1−s',1+s') × (−s',s') is Borel. (b) G is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞Z: by the sibling tangent_aesm (the accepted theorem Submission.imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm with n = 2, U = univ), x ↦ p_{T_x} is a.e.-strongly measurable for H²⌞M; μ = (H²⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ H²⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so it is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac) and for μ⌞Z (restrict). Evaluation (L, v) ↦ L v is continuous bilinear and x ↦ Ax is continuous, so x ↦ p_{T_x}(Ax) is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞Z (ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂ applied to the identity of the operator space); so is its squared norm, and division by the continuous function x ↦ |πx|² preserves a.e.-measurability (AEMeasurable.div), hence a.e.-strong measurability of the real-valued G.
3. (μ(Z) < ∞.) If x ∈ Z then |x| − 1 ≤ ||x| − 1| < s ≤ |s|, so Z ⊆ K := closedBall(0, 1 + |s|), which is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and Borel. By the definition of R.measure, μ(K) = ∫_K θ d(H²⌞M) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH² (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, Set.inter_comm), which is finite by the IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult (K compact, K ⊆ univ). Hence μ(Z) ≤ μ(K) < ∞ and μ⌞Z is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict).
4. ((i).) The hypothesis with b ≡ 1 gives ∫ H = ∫_Z ofReal(G) dμ ≤ ∫_Z 1 dμ = μ(Z) < ∞ (setLIntegral_mono with the measurable constant 1, using ofReal(G) ≤ 1 on Z from step 1; setLIntegral_const). Since H is a.e.-measurable with finite integral, H < ∞ a.e. (ae_lt_top').
5. ((ii).) H_ℝ = toReal∘H is a.e.-strongly measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_toReal) and nonnegative, and ∫ ofReal(H_ℝ) ≤ ∫ H < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le), so H_ℝ has finite integral (hasFiniteIntegral_iff_ofReal) and is integrable. By (i), ofReal(H_ℝ(p)) = H(p) for a.e. p (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
6. ((iii) for 0 ≤ β ≤ M.) Let β : ℝ² → ℝ be Borel with 0 ≤ β ≤ M. (a) p ↦ β(p)H_ℝ(p) is integrable (bounded measurable factor times an integrable function: Integrable.bdd_mul) and nonnegative; x ↦ β(F̃(x))G(x) is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞Z (step 2), nonnegative, and bounded by M·1 on Z (step 1), hence integrable for the finite measure μ⌞Z (Integrable.of_bound with ae_restrict_mem). (b) By integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae, ∫ βH_ℝ = toReal(∫ ofReal(β(p)H_ℝ(p)) dp) and ∫_Z β(F̃)G dμ = toReal(∫_Z ofReal(β(F̃(x))G(x)) dμ). (c) For a.e. p, ofReal(β(p)H_ℝ(p)) = ofReal(β(p))·ofReal(H_ℝ(p)) = ofReal(β(p))·H(p) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with β ≥ 0, and step 5). The hypothesis with the Borel function b := ofReal∘β gives ∫ ofReal(β)·H = ∫_Z ofReal(β(F̃(x)))·ofReal(G(x)) dμ = ∫_Z ofReal(β(F̃(x))G(x)) dμ. Hence the two lower integrals in (b) agree, and ∫ βH_ℝ = ∫_Z β(F̃)G dμ.
7. ((iii) in general.) Let b be Borel with |b| ≤ M (so M ≥ 0). Then b⁺ := max(b, 0) and b⁻ := max(−b, 0) are Borel with values in [0, M] and b = b⁺ − b⁻ (max_zero_sub_eq_self). Pointwise bH_ℝ = b⁺H_ℝ − b⁻H_ℝ and b(F̃)G = b⁺(F̃)G − b⁻(F̃)G, and the four functions on the right are integrable by step 6(a); by integral_sub and step 6, ∫ bH_ℝ = ∫ b⁺H_ℝ − ∫ b⁻H_ℝ = ∫_Z b⁺(F̃)G dμ − ∫_Z b⁻(F̃)G dμ = ∫_Z b(F̃)G dμ.
8. ((iv).) Let s' ≤ s and Sq := Sq(s'). Apply the hypothesis to the Borel function b := 1_{Sq} (indicator with value 1): ∫ 1_{Sq}·H = ∫_Z 1_{Sq}(F̃(x))·ofReal(G(x)) dμ. The left side is ∫_{Sq} H (1_{Sq}·H is the indicator of Sq applied to H; lintegral_indicator). On the right, 1_{Sq}(F̃(x)) = 1_{F̃⁻¹(Sq)}(x) and F̃⁻¹(Sq) is Borel (step 2(a)), so the right side equals ∫_{F̃⁻¹(Sq)} ofReal(G) d(μ⌞Z) = ∫_{F̃⁻¹(Sq) ∩ Z} ofReal(G) dμ (lintegral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict). Finally F̃⁻¹(Sq) ∩ Z = Z(s,s'): x ∈ F̃⁻¹(Sq) iff 1 − s' < |x| < 1 + s' and −s' < f(x) < s', i.e. ||x| − 1| < s' and |f(x)| < s' (abs_sub_lt_iff, abs_lt); since s' ≤ s these imply ||x| − 1| < s and |f(x)| < s, so the intersection is exactly {x : ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s', |x − πx| < s|x|} = Z(s,s'). This proves (iv). ∎
proof_key_steps: Self-adjointness of π and Bessel for (a, e): |p_{T_x}(Ax)| ≤ |Ax| ≤ |πx|, so 0 ≤ G ≤ 1 on {⟨x,a⟩ > 0}; G is μ⌞Z-a.e. strongly measurable via the reused tangent-projection measurability theorem and μ ≪ H²⌞M.
Z ⊆ closedBall(0, 1 + |s|) gives μ(Z) < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult); b ≡ 1 gives ∫H ≤ μ(Z) < ∞, so H < ∞ a.e. and toReal∘H is integrable.
For Borel 0 ≤ β ≤ M both sides of the identity with b = ofReal∘β are lower integrals of integrable nonnegative functions; convert them to Bochner integrals and split a bounded signed b = b⁺ − b⁻.
b = 1_{Sq(s')} together with F̃⁻¹(Sq(s')) ∩ Z(s,s) = Z(s,s') for s' ≤ s gives the box identity.

subproblems.title: Integrals against the weight of a cone current scale homogeneously
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) a cone (IsConeCurrent C: η_{0,λ#}C = C for every λ > 0) and R an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n) representing C, with weight μ := R.measure. Then for every r > 0 and every function φ : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ φ(rx) dμ(x) = (r^n)^{−1} ∫ φ dμ (Bochner integrals; no measurability or integrability of φ is assumed).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsConeCurrent C → R.Represents C → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → ∀ φ : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ x, φ (r • x) ∂R.measure = (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ x, φ x ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5(i) (Scaling) of the parent-supplied proof of idtp_cse_flux_density_eq.
1. Fix r > 0 and let S(x) := rx. S is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse x ↦ r^{−1}x (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r), hence a measurable equivalence e (Homeomorph.toMeasurableEquiv) with e x = rx.
2. (Image measure.) Claim: map S μ = ofReal((r^{−1})^n)·μ. By Measure.ext it suffices to compare both sides on Borel sets A. By Measure.map_apply (S measurable, A Borel), (map S μ)(A) = μ(S^{−1}(A)), and S^{−1}(A) = {x : rx ∈ A} = (y ↦ r^{−1}y)''A: if rx ∈ A then x = r^{−1}(rx), and conversely r(r^{−1}y) = y ∈ A (smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀, mul_inv_cancel₀). By the sibling cone_measure (the accepted theorem Submission.cone_current_imrep_measure_smul_image, applied with λ := r^{−1} > 0 and the Borel set A), μ((y ↦ r^{−1}y)''A) = ofReal((r^{−1})^n)·μ(A). Hence (map S μ)(A) = (ofReal((r^{−1})^n)·μ)(A) for every Borel A, proving the claim.
3. (Change of variables.) For every φ : ℝ^P → ℝ, integral_map_equiv for the measurable equivalence e (valid for arbitrary φ) gives ∫ φ d(map S μ) = ∫ φ(S x) dμ(x) = ∫ φ(rx) dμ(x). By step 2 and integral_smul_measure (also valid for arbitrary φ), ∫ φ(rx) dμ(x) = ∫ φ d(ofReal((r^{−1})^n)·μ) = toReal(ofReal((r^{−1})^n))·∫ φ dμ = (r^{−1})^n ∫ φ dμ (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, as (r^{−1})^n ≥ 0).

subproblems.title: A density equal to c·p₁ with box limit 4m equals m·p₁
subproblems.statement: Let 0 < s ≤ 1, c ∈ ℝ, m ∈ ℕ, H : ℝ² → [0,∞] and I : ℝ → [0,∞]. Put B := (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8) × (−s, s), B' := (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8) × (−s/8, s/8) and Sq(s') := (1 − s', 1 + s') × (−s', s'). Assume (a) H(p) < ∞ for Lebesgue-a.e. p; (b) toReal(H(p)) = c·p_1 for a.e. p ∈ B; (c) ∫_{Sq(s')} H dp = I(s') for every s' ∈ (0, s/8]; (d) I(s')/ofReal(s'²) → 4m in [0,∞] as s' → 0⁺. Then H(p) = ofReal(m·p_1) for a.e. p ∈ B'.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7 (c ≥ 0), 8 (c = m) and 9 (conclusion) of the parent-supplied proof of idtp_cse_flux_density_eq. Lebesgue measure on ℝ² is volume = volume.prod volume (Measure.volume_eq_prod); ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal.
1. (H = ofReal(c p_1) a.e. on B.) For a.e. p ∈ B, by (a) and (b), H(p) = ofReal(toReal(H(p))) = ofReal(c p_1) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
2. (c ≥ 0.) B' ⊆ B because s/8 ≤ s, and p_1 > 1 − s/8 ≥ 7/8 > 0 on B'. The Lebesgue measure of B' is (s/4)·(s/4) > 0 (Measure.prod_prod, Real.volume_Ioo). Suppose c < 0. For a.e. p ∈ B', (b) gives c p_1 = toReal(H(p)) ≥ 0, while c p_1 < 0; so a.e. p lies outside B', i.e. B' is Lebesgue-null (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem), a contradiction. Hence c ≥ 0.
3. (Box integrals.) Let 0 < s' ≤ s/8. Then Sq(s') ⊆ B (1 − s/8 ≤ 1 − s' and s' ≤ s), Sq(s') is Borel, and by step 1 (setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae) I(s') = ∫_{Sq(s')} H dp = ∫_{Sq(s')} ofReal(c p_1) dp. By Tonelli on the product of intervals (Measure.prod_restrict, lintegral_prod), ∫_{Sq(s')} ofReal(c p_1) dp = ∫_{(1−s',1+s')} ofReal(ct)·λ((−s', s')) dt = ofReal(2s')·∫_{(1−s',1+s')} ofReal(ct) dt. Since t ↦ ct is continuous, hence integrable on the bounded interval, and nonnegative there (c ≥ 0 and t > 1 − s' ≥ 7/8 > 0), ∫_{(1−s',1+s')} ofReal(ct) dt = ofReal(∫_{1−s'}^{1+s'} ct dt) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal) = ofReal(c·((1 + s')² − (1 − s')²)/2) = ofReal(2cs') (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul, integral_id). Hence I(s') = ofReal(2s')·ofReal(2cs') = ofReal(4c)·ofReal(s'²) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, c ≥ 0).
4. (c = m.) For 0 < s' ≤ s/8, ofReal(s'²) is neither 0 nor ∞, so I(s')/ofReal(s'²) = ofReal(4c) (ENNReal.mul_div_cancel_right). Since (0, s/8] ∈ 𝓝[>]0 (Ioc_mem_nhdsGT, s/8 > 0), the function s' ↦ I(s')/ofReal(s'²) is eventually equal to the constant ofReal(4c) along 𝓝[>]0, hence tends to ofReal(4c) (tendsto_const_nhds.congr'). The filter 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ is nontrivial and [0,∞] is Hausdorff, so (d) and uniqueness of limits (tendsto_nhds_unique) give ofReal(4c) = 4m = ofReal(4m) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_natCast). Since 4c ≥ 0 and 4m ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_eq_ofReal_iff gives 4c = 4m, i.e. c = m.
5. (Conclusion.) For a.e. p ∈ B' ⊆ B, steps 1 and 4 give H(p) = ofReal(c p_1) = ofReal(m p_1). ∎

Tonelli: ∫_{Sq(s')} ofReal(c p_1) dp = ofReal(4c)·ofReal(s'²), so I(s')/ofReal(s'²) = ofReal(4c) for 0 < s' ≤ s/8.
Uniqueness of limits along 𝓝[>]0 gives ofReal(4c) = 4m, hence c = m and H = ofReal(m p_1) a.e. on B'.
